title: On-chain fundamentals
label: Module 1
subtitle: Wallet, RPC, fee, gas, tip and slippage. What every button actually does before you press it.

lessons.title: How a Solana transaction really happens
lessons.description: From the click to the confirmed block: what gets signed, who relays it and where it can silently die.

lessons.title: Wallets, seed phrases and the keys you must never paste
lessons.description: Custody in practice — what lives on your device, what lives on the chain, and the exact moment people lose everything.

lessons.title: Fee, gas and priority tip
lessons.description: Three numbers people mix up. What each one pays for and which of them decides whether you land the block.

lessons.title: RPC, latency and why you arrive late
lessons.description: The gap between a public RPC and a dedicated one, measured in milliseconds, and what that means when fifteen wallets fight over the same block.

lessons.title: Slippage: the setting that eats your entry
lessons.description: Why a wide tolerance turns a good entry into a bad one, and how to size it against real liquidity.

lessons.title: Reading a transaction on the explorer
lessons.description: Instructions, transfers and program logs — the three panes that tell you what actually happened.

title: Working the Radar
label: Module 2
subtitle: Sources, channels, call owners, tier and voice. Pulling signal out of 1,542 messages a day.

lessons.title: Setting up your first sources
lessons.description: Which channels are worth listening to and how to tell a call apart from noise on day one.

lessons.title: Tiers: who lands it, who repeats it, who only talks
lessons.description: The classification behind the feed and how it changes what deserves your attention.

lessons.title: Call owners and attribution
lessons.description: Who called it first, who copied it, and why that order is the whole story.

lessons.title: Alerts that are worth waking up for
lessons.description: Building filters that fire rarely and mean something when they do.

lessons.title: Reading the feed under pressure
lessons.description: What to look at first when three calls land in the same minute.

lessons.title: Squads: organising who you follow
lessons.description: Grouping wallets by behaviour instead of by name, and why that survives contact with reality.

title: Read a token in 60 seconds
label: Module 3
subtitle: LP, dev, top 10, snipers, insiders and bundlers. The Rick Bot X-ray, taken apart.

lessons.title: Liquidity: how much and whose
lessons.description: Where the pool came from, whether it is locked, and what happens the second it is not.

lessons.title: The dev wallet and its history
lessons.description: What the deployer did before this token, and why that is the single fastest read available.

lessons.title: Top 10 holders and concentration
lessons.description: Reading the distribution without fooling yourself with wallets that belong to the same person.

lessons.title: Snipers, insiders and bundlers
lessons.description: Three patterns in the first block that decide whether there is a trade here at all.

lessons.title: Mint, freeze and the authorities that matter
lessons.description: The permissions still held by the contract and what each one lets someone do to you.

lessons.title: The 60-second checklist, end to end
lessons.description: Running the whole read on a live token, in order, out loud.

title: Exit & post-trade
label: Module 4
subtitle: Position sizing, partial exits and the log that turns a trade into a lesson.

lessons.title: Sizing before you are excited
lessons.description: Deciding the number while it is still cheap to be honest about it.

lessons.title: Partial exits without regret
lessons.description: Taking the position off in pieces, and why the first piece is the one that matters.

lessons.title: Stops that survive volatility
lessons.description: Placing the invalidation where the thesis dies, not where the chart looks scary.

lessons.title: The trade log
lessons.description: What to write down at the close so the next trade is different from this one.

lessons.title: Reading your own numbers
lessons.description: Turning your PnL history into two or three decisions you can actually change.
